prompt: Let $f(x) = 3x$ and $g(x) = x + 5$. Write $f(g(x))$ as a simplified expression.
hint: Instead of a number, the inside machine now hands over a whole expression: $g(x) = x + 5$.

hints.text: Instead of a number, the inside machine now hands over a whole expression: $g(x) = x + 5$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $f(x) = 2x$ and $g(x) = x + 1$. Then $f(g(x)) = 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2$. Same method: drop the inside expression into $f$, then distribute.
Feed $x + 5$ into $f$: you get $3(x + 5)$. Now distribute the 3.

explanation: The outside machine triples whatever it gets: $3(x + 5)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with a number
steps: Now test the expression: $3(2) + 15 = 21$. It matches.
Testing one number is a fast way to catch a mistake in the distributing.
